weil-mclain.notes: Age is decoded from the 7-digit CP number on a separate tag/sticker, NOT from the serial number. Page states the chart is a 'guideline for approximate manufacture year' (1988 into 2023), so every band is approximate:true. Bands 1988-2008 are printed in full and are consecutive with no gaps or overlaps. Bands 2009-2022 are printed with masked xxx endings/beginnings (e.g. 6150xxx); the file expands each xxx prefix to its full 1000-number block, so every CP in a shared-prefix block falls in two bands and must decode to 'cannot determine', never first-match. 2023 device band: the chart prints 2023 as beginning 8067xxx with ending '???', so its entire known range coincides with 2022's ending block; the 8067000-8067999 band for 2023 exists ONLY to force 'cannot determine' on that block, it is not a true 2023 range, and CPs above 8067999 match zero bands (2023 continuation and 2024+ unknown from this chart). Fallback if device bands are rejected: truncate 2022 to max 8066999 and drop 2023. NORMALIZATION (resolved): locked normalization strips spaces, so the prose form 'CP 2530051' normalizes to 'CP2530051'; pattern ^CP\d{7}$ with year positions [2,9] is therefore correct. CAVEATS: AquaBalance model CP numbers are NOT sequential and the chart may not suffice for them (serial alone cannot distinguish them); 6-digit CP numbers are generally early-1980s and prior and the page directs techs to contact Weil-McLain (pattern covers 7-digit only; zero-padded 6-digit values fall below the chart and correctly do not match). Page header misspells parent as 'Marely-Wylain'; history section spelling 'Marley-Wylain' used here. Page header lists Williamson Thermoflo as a related brand; sharing of the CP system is NOT verified, so it is not listed as a sister.

styles.notes: Example CP2530051 is the page's format example (text + data-plate photo, Model GU-4, Series No. 2 — the '2' is a series number, not a year); its year 1993 is chart-derived (2530051 falls in 2400000-2609500), not page-stated. No other example serial appears on the page.

york.notes: Style-1 year uses split-year extraction as an ordered list of half-open ranges [[1,2],[3,4]] whose sliced digits concatenate ('0'+'5'='05') before the century rule; style-2 year uses a dual-candidate letter table whose values are either a single full year (exactly one year) or a two-element candidate list (21-year cycle, both years, never a guessed pick). MONTH CONFLICT RESOLVED FOR YORK: both York charts (style 1 and style 2) map K to September, agreeing with Coleman and with Luxaire's style-4 table; Luxaire's own style-1 chart (K October) remains the sole outlier and is a Luxaire-internal inconsistency, not a York question — York's decode of W0K5896070 is September 2005. No usesStylesOf: York's two styles are defined here in full; Coleman and Luxaire share these two systems (same sample serials, same tables, same October 2004 boundary) but each carries additional numeric styles, so reuse would be wrong in both directions. Parent note: the page names Johnson Controls International as parent and records Bosch's July 2024 agreement to buy the residential/light-commercial HVAC business (sale slated within ~12 months); completion status is not verified on this page (last updated 12/26/2024), so the parent field keeps Johnson Controls International. Quirk: the style-2 data-plate image header reads 'Style 4 Data Plate' although the page text numbers this system Style 2; the plate serial is the same WAKM011379, so this is a legacy image label, not a third style. PARENTHETICAL-PREFIX EDGE, NOT ENCODED: the page cautions that some serials of this style begin with a letter in parentheses, e.g. (S)EBHM062202, meaning 'ignore the first letter in parenthesis' (decodes as EBHM062202: February, 1978 or 1999); the locked normalization strips spaces/dashes only, so that literal input would not match this pattern — left in notes only, deliberately not a formal example, so the builder's every-example-must-decode rule is not broken.

styles.notes: Split-year: 2nd character (index 1) and 4th character (index 3) are the two year digits, split around the month letter; the chart states this explicitly ('The 2nd digit is a 0 and the 4th digit is a 5 ... Combined they read 05 which is equivalent to the year 2005'). Position 0 is the plant letter (chart table: A Apodaca, N Norman, S Source One, W Wichita; not validated by the pattern). Positions 4-9 are a six-digit sequence. Month letters skip I and J. yearFloor 2004 reflects the documented October 2004 start: with this floor, YY=05 resolves to 2005 only and a pre-2004 YY cannot match this style.

21-year cycle, dual-candidate letters A-N (13 letters): first cycle 1971-1991, second cycle 1992-2004, truncated at N=2004 because the style ended October 2004. Single-year letters P-Y (1984-1991) are first-cycle only; their second-cycle years (2005-2012) never occurred under this style, so they decode exactly, never as candidates. Year letters skip I, O, Q, U, Z. Position 0 is the plant letter (chart table: A Addison, B Blackville, C Canada, D Medina, E Elyra, M Madyville, N Norman, W Wichita, X Mexico, Y York). Position 3 is the item type (M Mfg Basic Unit, P Purchased Basic Unit, S Mfg Low Side Item, T Purchased Low Side Item, Y Mfg Accessory, Z Purchased Accessory, O Filler). Positions 4-9 are a six-digit sequence.
